record_type: Historical source identity, reading observations and bounded retrieval coverage
purpose: Second September 11 private AUTODIN II source batch: Western Union revision history/comparison, SRI/ISI correspondence discovery, INWG alternatives, DCA decision records, and DDN security interfaces.
evidence_policy: Separate requirement, recommendation, specified interface, static implementation, reported test, measured behavior, operational deployment, catalog lead and unsuccessful retrieval. OCR supports discovery; decisive scanned passages use original images. Native ASCII is read directly. Original files remain intact; public sources are linked, with temporary downloads and derived research extracts separately recorded.

decisive_sections.paraphrase: Red interface supports a host or gateway.
IP header gives actual Red IP destination; X.25 DDN RVN address may identify a gateway next hop for IP devices not directly attached to a BFE.

additional_context_read.paraphrase: Revised IP security option and MIL-STD-1777 change 1; security option required first.
Multiple host ports require separate BFEs and IP addresses; host selects BFE. This is not demonstrated connection continuity.

documents.conclusion_limits: Provides a later specified accommodation for the address distinction criticized in 1986. Cannot date initial introduction, identify author/cause, show adoption in response to BBN, establish AUTODIN II ancestry, or demonstrate deployment.

original_image_inspections.passage_or_paraphrase: Final Computer Program Development Specification; original March 5, 1979 and three revision dates; document and contract identifiers.
Revision 1 replacement-page list, July 4, 1979. This is not the superseded edition.
Revision 2 replacement-page list, August 3, 1979. This is not the superseded edition.
February 8, 1980: Title, 10, 18, 30, B1, C1, C44, D4. Page 18 is visually present although OCR omitted it.
Distinguishes TCP-TCP network protocol, CCU/TAC event interfaces, and MCCU implementation examples.
Explicit references to the July 15, 1976 SRI TCP and THP specifications.
Revision-3 error behavior, including new non-retransmitted SYN on an established connection, error transmission, and closure.
CCU has one network subscriber address; TCP ports demultiplex user/host channels and supply user identity.
One connection security value; 512 TCC codes; 16-bit subscriber address; 1/11/4 static-dynamic/user/function port division; preemptible flag.
OPEN authorization for requested S/P/T without validating remote subscriber/port addresses; OPEN initializes state, SEND begins handshake.
SIP extracts S/P/T from BSL. Specified security/TCC must match; unspecified values need authorization. Directional precedence may differ, with higher value used for preemption.
Higher-category authorized SYN may preempt a marked established connection at an occupied local socket; category I protected; old TCB closed and new handshake.
Resource exhaustion permits connection preemption as last resort; lowest category first, never category I.
Fixed 29-byte header, no format variation; unused fields zero; illustration uses DEC memory order.
Four-bit VER field without explicit protocol-version value; 31-bit sequence-number definition and header control definitions.
Eight-bit source/destination network fields currently zero; 16-bit subscriber and port components.
Two-byte checksum field reserved and unused by CCU/TAC/NCC TCPs.
Control repertoire includes errors, out-of-band interrupt/status. No DSN operation in the defined repertoire.
OPEN event represents TCC in a 16-bit parameter and prints range 0-512.
TCP/SIP Send Data event represents security and precedence with eight bits each, TCC with sixteen; TCC range printed 0-512.
BSL/TCP/THP layout without IP leader; nine bits per TCC copy, four per security copy; checksum unused note.
Title and opening of memorandum of agreement on transfer of ARPANET management to DCA; proposed July 1, 1975 effective date.
Clauses k-l: coordinated experimentation and DCA-authorized AUTODIN II concept tests.
Typed Paschall and Heilmeier names; blank signatures and dates. Execution not established.
Entered March 25, 1975 at 14:15; NLS source RUSSELL,DCAAGREEMENT.NLS;9, dated February 28, 1975 at 13:56.
June 23 heading, June 22 journal entry. January 9, 1975 D. ARPA memorandum and June 1975 DTACCS memorandum cited; latter day clipped.
Paragraph 5 attributes reliability and cost advantages of distributed switching to a June 1975 Network Analysis Corporation study; study itself not recovered.
July 16, 1976 raw NLS proposal ISU 76-136, Network Operating System Study; RADC RFP F30602-76-R-0299.
Qualifications describe TCP/THP specification work, DCA100-76-C-0034, February-June 1976, Postel as principal investigator.

Complete references page cites INWG General Note 72; Tomlinson and Dalal sequence-number notes; Dalal connection-establishment note; Cerf TCP Resynchronization, SU-DSL Technical Note 79, January 1976. INWG 96 not listed on this page.
Moving fragmentation/reassembly into a separate IP gaining favor; too large a change for TCP-3, considered for TCP-4.
Speech/conferencing, low delay, unreliable service, and transit-service mapping are contemporaneous concerns; passage does not attribute them to AUTODIN II.
DCA cost/schedule study due April 1979; Gerald P. Dinneen signature.
Ratification and implementation arrangements; AUTODIN II transition to standards after initial operational capability.
DCA 1000 technical and DCA 500 configuration responsibilities; panel, control board, and steering group organization.
Responsibilities and transition of leadership from research to operations as protocol standardization matures.
PSTP membership including NBS and intelligence community ex officio; DCEC facilities including EDN for testing.
INWG 96 cover; July 1975; London July 29, 1975; CCITT contribution September 1975; Cerf, McKenzie, Scantlebury, Zimmermann.
Virtual host, transport station, and shared proposal context.
Transport subscriber explicitly distinguished from packet-network subscriber; 16-bit port, local mapping, at least four low port bits.
Datagram and transport headers may overlap or be separately encapsulated where a common standard datagram is unavailable.
Optional letter checksum incompletely defined; user services include lettergrams and liaisons.
Further-study discussion of reliable interruption, sequence, flow control, and purging unprocessed data.

corrections_and_conclusions.claim: Western Union continued a distinct, modified AUTODIN II branch into February 1980.
corrections_and_conclusions.details: Explicit SRI references; 29-byte header, zero network fields, unused checksum and BSL/TCP boundary coexist with changed fixed connection security, nine-bit TCC copies, and explicit connection preemption. RFC 760/761 supply the January 1980 standards comparison.

corrections_and_conclusions.claim: Continuity of security/precedence/TCC requirements is selective, with incompatible formats and rules.
corrections_and_conclusions.details: SRI/BBN eight-bit TCC, Western Union nine-bit copies, RFC 760 two security bits and eight-bit TCC, later RFC 791 24-bit TCC. Western Union 512-count versus 0-512 event range remains an unresolved internal discrepancy.

corrections_and_conclusions.claim: Journal 32190 and 36044 are now identified beyond OCR leads.
corrections_and_conclusions.details: Unsigned agreement and different-project research proposal; neither proves an executed agreement, AUTODIN II tests, or recovered contract/SOW.

corrections_and_conclusions.claim: Broader INWG ideas and contemporary TCP design concerns qualify exclusive or single-cause origin claims.
corrections_and_conclusions.status: Direct proposals and meeting record, with causal limits
corrections_and_conclusions.details: Transport/network customer distinction, port allocation and modular interfaces circulated across projects. SRI cites wider INWG work, not INWG 96 on its complete references page. No explicit AUTODIN II-to-split decision link recovered.

corrections_and_conclusions.claim: The 1978/1980 DCA decisions can be dated and bounded more precisely.
corrections_and_conclusions.details: Cost analysis due April 1979; April 3, 1980 ratification allows AUTODIN II post-IOC transition and defines implementation/panel responsibilities. Actual study, minutes and explanation remain missing.

corrections_and_conclusions.claim: The 1986 KI-111 address restriction cannot be described as permanently unchanged.
corrections_and_conclusions.status: Later specified accommodation, not deployment or causal history
corrections_and_conclusions.details: March 1989 section 2.4.3 permits a distinct next-hop gateway address. Earlier guide and ICD revisions needed to determine when/how this entered the specification and whether it descended from AUTODIN II.
